newItems.prompt: A controller reads an eight-bit sensor value through eight shared conductors while a separate select line enables the sensor output. What do these conductors represent?
choices: A parallel data bus plus a control/select signal
A single serial transmit pin carrying eight bits one at a time
Eight independent power rails and no data paths
A clock network that cannot carry sensor values
newItems.explanation: The eight data conductors form a parallel bus; the select signal determines when one device is permitted to drive the shared conductors. Bus design must prevent simultaneous drivers and meet timing and logic-level requirements.

Fine-stranded conductor with appropriately rated flexible insulation
Coaxial cable with the shield used as a substitute for an insulation jacket
Any solid conductor so long as resistance is low
newItems.explanation: Many small strands improve flex life. Conductor cross-section, insulation temperature/voltage rating, connector type and mechanical strain relief must still match the application.

newItems.prompt: Two copper conductors of equal length and material are labeled 18 AWG and 24 AWG. Which conclusion is correct before considering installation or insulation ratings?
choices: 24 AWG has greater copper cross-sectional area
18 AWG has greater copper area and typically lower DC resistance
Both have identical conductor diameters because AWG describes insulation only
AWG numbering directly specifies a universal permissible current independent of temperature
newItems.explanation: In American Wire Gauge, lower gauge number means larger nominal conductor diameter. The 18 AWG conductor has more area and generally less DC resistance at the same length and temperature; ampacity depends on additional installation conditions.

newItems.prompt: A 50-ohm coaxial transmission line is cut to half its original length but retains the same geometry and dielectric. What happens to its nominal characteristic impedance?
choices: It doubles to 100 ohms
It falls to 25 ohms
It remains approximately 50 ohms
It changes unpredictably whenever length changes
newItems.explanation: Characteristic impedance is primarily determined by distributed inductance and capacitance per unit length, Z0≈√(L′/C′) for a low-loss line. Length changes total attenuation and phase delay, not the line’s nominal Z0.

newItems.prompt: A shielded cable connects two devices. Why must a technician distinguish protective earthing from signal-reference or shield bonding?
choices: Shield braid is always allowed to replace protective earthing
Protective earth is a safety fault-current path, while signal/shield bonding serves noise and reference functions and follows equipment specifications
Any single thin drain wire is always sufficient for mains fault current
A shield should always be cut at both ends regardless of the product design
newItems.explanation: Protective earthing is a required safety function for specified equipment. Shield and signal-return design depends on interference frequencies, geometry and grounding scheme; it cannot be substituted for the protective-conductor requirements.

newItems.prompt: A technician splices a coaxial run, and the receiver develops reflections despite a DC continuity pass. What detail is most likely responsible?
choices: The splice restores center conductor only and ignores dielectric geometry and shield continuity
The center conductor and shield remain separated by intact rated dielectric
A connector designed for the cable retains its nominal impedance
The splice maintains shield coverage and strain relief
newItems.explanation: At RF a coax splice must retain the center conductor, dielectric spacing, coaxial shield continuity and compatible impedance. A continuity test cannot prove low reflection or return loss.

newItems.prompt: A 50 Ω transmitter feedline is terminated by a purely resistive 200 Ω antenna input. Neglecting loss, what is the magnitude of the voltage reflection coefficient?
choices: 0, because all resistive loads are matched
newItems.explanation: For real impedances, |Γ|=|(ZL−Z0)/(ZL+Z0)|=|(200−50)/(200+50)|=150/250=0.6. Strong mismatch reflects a fraction |Γ|²=0.36 of incident power; ordinary line losses can hide some reflection at the meter.
